## 3. Runtime and constraints

Compiled by `pyc.py` for `py_core`; only this subset is allowed (anything else is rejected at compile time):

```text
ints, True/False/None, names, + - & | ^ << >> ~ unary -, not/and/or
  in conditions, one comparison per expression (< <= > >= == !=),
  mem32[addr] loads/stores (also mem32[a] op= v), name op= expr,
  if/elif/else, while/break/continue, pass, global, import (ignored).
  "from <name> import *" where <name>.py sits next to the source file
  inlines that file there (once), so firmware can be split into modules
  that share one global namespace; errors name the original file / line.
  Without such a file, "from <name> import *" reads the SystemVerilog
  package <name>.sv found next to the source or in a -I directory (the
  memory map packages, e.g. video_processor_map_pkg.sv): its
  "localparam ... NAME = expr;" lines become UPPER_CASE constants NAME
  (folded), "import <pkg>::*;" loads that package first, <pkg>::NAME and
  SV literals (32'h0001_0000, 'h40, 16'd10) are understood, so the
  firmware takes its addresses from the same file as the RTL decoders.
  UPPER_CASE module-level names bound once to a constant expression
  (or const(expr)) are folded at compile time.
  def f(a, b): ... return x   functions with positional parameters,
  called as f(x, y) in expressions or statements; recursion is allowed
  up to the core's call depth. Missing return -> None.
  A function passed to irq_handler() is an interrupt handler instead:
  no parameters, no return value, cannot be called directly.
Builtins: irq_handler(fn), irq_enable(), irq_disable(), halt(value).
Strings: a string literal (in any expression, e.g. puts("text")) is a
  small int handle; the text goes to a string table in flash at
  STR_BASE (0x8000), outside the boot image, for the firmware to read at
  run time through the flash controller. The table has 512 slots of 64
  bytes (0x8000-0xFFFF): [0] length (0..62), [1] 1 if the string
  continues in the next slot, [2..] the bytes. A handle is the first slot
  number; slots 128..255 are emitted as h - 256 so they fit LOAD_SMALL,
  slots 256..511 as h (a constant). Firmware decodes a handle with
  slot = h if h >= 256 else h & 255.
  strings("a", "b", ...) returns the handle of a block of consecutive
  one-slot strings (each <= 62 bytes), so handle + i selects entry i (a
  block never straddles slot 256, so the decoding holds for handle + i).
  Identical strings share slots.
Not in the hardware fast path (rejected): * / % ** on variables,
default/keyword arguments, closures, lists, dicts, floats, classes.
```

- Register addresses come from the SystemVerilog map packages (`from <pkg> import *`), never hard-coded numbers, so firmware and RTL decoders share one source.
- Every hardware wait has a bound (poll count) and reports a timeout instead of hanging.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference program's documentation):

```text
video_processor firmware: the object detectors and the multi-target tracking state machine.

NTRK object_tracker detectors, one per object class (video_processor_map_pkg: detector c at
TRK + c * TRK_STRIDE). The classes to detect (det_mask, bit c), the box style of each and the most
targets tracked at any time (max_targets) come from the camera's control registers 0x50-0x55
(camera.py camera_detect). Each detector finds the pixels that look like its class (detect_setup):
  0 pedestrian  luma below 80 (a dark figure on a light scene), runs of 2+ pixels
  1 face        skin tone: Y 50-235, Cb 77-127, Cr 135-175, saturation 12+, runs 3 .. W/6
  2 automobile  saturated paint: Y 30-235, saturation 40+, runs W/16 .. W/3
  3 vehicle     the same paint in runs wider than W/3 (bus, truck, tram)
(W = frame width; a run is judged by its whole length) and groups them into up to NBLOB separate
objects per frame (blobs: BLOB_X / BLOB_Y / BLOB_N; specks smaller than the class's least size are
dropped by the hardware, BLOB_CFG.KEEP). The CPU checks the shape of each blob (class_ok: enough
pixels; a pedestrian at least as tall as wide and at most a quarter of the frame wide; a face about
as tall as it is wide; vehicles wider than tall; a face or a car at most half the frame wide). This
is a feature (colour, size, shape) detector, not a trained classifier. Each class has its own
detector, so a person inside a vehicle (a driver's face behind the windscreen) is found by the face
detector whatever the vehicle detectors find around it.

Tracking, per class: up to NTR targets (tracks), each SEARCH (free) -> TRACK (matched to a blob)
-> COAST (missed: the box keeps moving with the velocity) -> back to free after TRK_LOST misses in
a row. Every frame each live track takes the nearest unused blob of its class within its gate
(box width + height + TRK_GATE around its predicted centre); blobs left over start new tracks while
fewer than max_targets targets (all classes together) are tracked. A track's state lives in its
detector's SCRATCH words (TW words per track, sc_get / sc_set), so one set of functions serves
every class and track. Centres and velocities are kept x 2 (x0 + x1); the box size grows at once
but shrinks by a quarter of the difference per frame, so everything is adds and shifts (py_core has
no multiply or divide). pred_lo / pred_hi give the predicted box for the next frame.
```

Per function:

```text
det_base: Address of class c's detector: TRK + c * TRK_STRIDE.

track_word: First SCRATCH word of track k (k * TW).

class_min: Fewest pixels of a target of class c (also the blobs' BLOB_CFG.KEEP).

detect_setup: Detector of class c: its look, the frame size, the whole frame searched, blobs, every track
free.

tracker_setup: Every selected class's detector set up (the others off), no target tracked.

mul: a * b for a, b >= 0 by shift and add (py_core has no multiply).

class_ok: Enough pixels and the shape of class c: a solid object (pixels at least 1/3 of the box, 1/4 for
vehicles) that is not the scene itself (at most 3/4 of the frame wide and half its height,
touching at most one frame border: a textured scene or a moving camera gives one huge blob).

in_target: True when (x, y) lies in the predicted box of a target of class c.

blob_ok: True when blob i of detector t has the shape of class c.

smooth_size: Grow to the measured size at once, shrink by a quarter of the difference.

track_step: One frame of the track at SCRATCH word b of detector t (i: the blob of its target, -1 when
missed): the new state, read from and saved to the SCRATCH words.

An alpha-beta tracker (Kalata, IEEE Trans. AES 1984) with alpha = 1 and beta = 1/2: the centre
takes the measured blob centre (no position smoothing: the blob box is already a clean
measurement), the velocity moves half way to the measured displacement, v = (v + (z - x)) / 2;
a missed target coasts with its velocity until TRK_LOST misses. Association (nearest_blob) is
gated greedy nearest neighbour in track order, a cheap stand-in for global nearest neighbour
(Bar-Shalom & Fortmann 1988) that is enough for the few, mostly separated targets per class.

nearest_blob: The unused blob of class c nearest the predicted centre of the track at word b, within its
gate; -1 when none.

pred_lo: Low edge of the predicted box: centre c (x 2) moved by v, half of size below it.
```

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the program.

```text
// Industry reference check - tracker.py (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] P. R. Kalata, "The Tracking Index: A Generalized Parameter for alpha-beta and alpha-
//   beta-gamma Target Trackers", IEEE Trans. AES 20(2):174-182, 1984; summary
//   https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_beta_filter (x_p = x + v T; r = z - x_p; x += alpha r;
//   v += beta r / T)
//   [2] Y. Bar-Shalom, T. E. Fortmann, "Tracking and Data Association", Academic Press 1988;
//   global vs greedy nearest-neighbour association with gating,
//   https://pytcl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/data_association.html
// Published algorithm / rules:
//   alpha-beta tracker: predict x_p = x + v, residual r = z - x_p, x = x_p + alpha r, v = v +
//   beta r (0 < alpha, beta <= 1; smaller gains smooth noise, larger follow manoeuvres);
//   association of measurements to tracks by gated nearest neighbour (greedy per track, or
//   global assignment).
// Comparison with this program (section 6):
//   Matches the structure: constant-velocity prediction, gate (size + TRK_GATE), coast on
//   misses, track dropped after TRK_LOST misses. Differs: alpha = 1 (the position jumps to the
//   measurement, no smoothing) and v = (v + (z - x)) / 2, i.e. beta = 1/2 of the residual;
//   association is greedy per track in slot order, not a global assignment, so two close
//   targets can swap.
// RESOLVED(REF-TRACKER-1) [LOW] Filter gains and association. Resolution: 2026-10-16:
//   documented in track_step's docstring (alpha = 1, beta = 1/2, Kalata 1984; greedy gated
//   nearest neighbour as a stand-in for GNN, Bar-Shalom & Fortmann 1988); behaviour kept.
```
